content:
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP & Document AI
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine learning engineer with 5+ years of experience in NLP, document classification and predictive modeling, including deploying and operating ML systems in production. Experienced in taking language-model and classification work from dataset preparation and experimentation through model serving and production monitoring. Currently pursuing a PhD focused on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts. Hands-on experience with Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, MLflow and Azure.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
- Developed and deployed a document classifier for scanned public-administration documents, achieving 94% accuracy and 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes; the service processes approximately 15,000 documents per day.
- Fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić transformer models for document classification and named entity recognition in Croatian administrative texts.
- Served models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service, using Azure ML and MLflow for experimentation tracking and model registry.
- Built production monitoring with weekly reports on input text length, vocabulary and predicted class distribution; an alert on PSI above 0.2 helped identify an OCR change that reduced accuracy by 9 percentage points, which was resolved within a week.
- Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 Croatian administrative documents with annotation guidelines and two annotators, achieving inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.87.
- Mentor two students during internships.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021–02/2023
- Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Built a customer complaint topic-classification solution, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic-regression baseline to fastText; the 11-topic classification supported weekly reporting to customer-service management.
- Produced SQL reports from an Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava
10/2020–08/2021
- Created a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated documents; wrote supporting Python scripts.

SELECTED PROJECT
Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
- Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using a sentence-embedding model, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
- Prototype only; checked manually and not used in production.

EDUCATION
PhD in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts. Expected completion: 2027.

MSc in Computer Science (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava | 2020

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, SQL, pandas, NumPy, Oracle SQL
Machine learning and NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, sentence-transformers, FAISS
Production and MLOps: MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently, PostgreSQL, Git, Linux
Annotation: Label Studio

CERTIFICATION
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024

TEACHING
Guest lecturer, NLP Summer School | 2025 | 90-minute lecture

PUBLICATION
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). “Named Entity Recognition for Croatian Administrative Documents.” Workshop on Slavic Language Processing.

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) | English (C1) | German (B2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear Machine Learning Engineer positioning and good evidence of production impact. The strongest content includes quantified outcomes: 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 23 classes, approximately 15,000 documents per day, 4,000 annotated documents, κ = 0.87, and a documented 9-point accuracy impact from an OCR change. The document also responsibly distinguishes the RAG work as a prototype rather than implying production experience. The summary, reverse-chronological experience, skills, certification, publication, and education sections are professional and easy to scan. Minor content limitations are that some relevant engineering details are presented in the skills list rather than tied to specific work achievements, and the distinction between the candidate’s ML Engineer experience and earlier Data Scientist experience could be clearer when assessed against the employer’s four-year ML-engineering requirement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible in content: it uses standard headings, conventional job titles, relevant keywords such as Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, model serving, production monitoring, MLflow, Azure ML, FastAPI, Docker, and RAG, and includes both expanded and recognizable technology names. The likely AI/ATS screening probability is high, approximately 88–92%, for the requirements supported by the candidate’s background. The RAG project is particularly valuable because it supplies the exact retrieval-augmented generation keyword. To improve matching further, the document should make supported terms such as model serving, model registry, production monitoring, data preparation, and model evaluation more explicit in the experience bullets. It should not add data versioning, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, orchestration, CI/CD, or automated testing because these are not supported by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the role’s NLP, document AI, language-model, model-serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, and MLOps expectations. It demonstrates taking models from dataset preparation and experimentation through deployment and monitoring, which matches the team’s prototype-to-production responsibilities. The customer complaint topic-classification work is also relevant to customer-support automation. The RAG requirement is shown through the personal question-answering prototype, but the CV correctly makes clear that it was not production software. The candidate’s material shows gaps against the stated requirement for at least four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; the documented ML Engineer role begins in March 2023, while the earlier Data Scientist role is not described as production ML engineering. The material also does not establish data versioning, feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines. These are requirement gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The degree, Azure, Python, MLflow/MLOps, model serving, and monitoring requirements are clearly supported.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, change the sentence “Experienced in taking language-model and classification work from dataset preparation and experimentation through model serving and production monitoring” to “Experienced in taking NLP and classification models from dataset preparation and experimentation through model evaluation, model serving, and production monitoring.” This uses the job ad’s terminology while remaining supported by the documented metrics, deployment, and monitoring work.

2. In the Professional Experience section under “Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o.”, revise the Azure/MLflow bullet to make the production engineering keywords more prominent: “Served models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry.” Keep the existing technologies, but place “model serving,” “experiment tracking,” and “model registry” in the wording rather than relying only on the skills section.

3. In the same Slavonica role, revise the dataset bullet to explicitly connect the work to large text-data preparation: “Prepared and annotated a 4,000-document Croatian administrative-text dataset, established annotation guidelines, and coordinated two annotators, achieving inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.87.” This better matches the job’s requirement to prepare and clean large text datasets without claiming unsupported data-ingestion or data-versioning experience.

4. In the Selected Project section, change the RAG project title to “Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Question-Answering Demo” and retain the sentence “Prototype only; checked manually and not used in production.” This puts the exact ATS term “RAG” and its expansion in the title while preserving the important truthful limitation.

5. In the Technical Skills section, consider grouping the supported tools under more job-relevant labels: “Programming: Python, SQL”; “ML/NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy”; “MLOps and production: MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently, Git, Linux”; “Data and annotation: pandas, NumPy, Oracle SQL, PostgreSQL, Label Studio.” Do not add data versioning, Airflow, Kubeflow, feature engineering, or data-ingestion pipelines, as these are not supported by the candidate information.
